Whether `holidays` may contain non-date values or datetimes is unspecified; I assume only date values are supplied and no validation of `holidays` is required.
Whether duplicate entries in `holidays` are allowed is unspecified; I assume they are harmless (treated as a set).
Whether `holidays` may be a one-shot iterator (generator) that is consumed is unspecified; I assume the implementation may materialize it into a set once.
Whether `holidays` may be None is unspecified; I assume None is not supported and would raise TypeError naturally.
Whether a `datetime.datetime` in `holidays` should match the corresponding date is unspecified; I assume holidays are plain dates and no normalization is required.
Whether `n` may be an int subclass other than bool (e.g. IntEnum) is unspecified; I assume only bool is explicitly rejected and other int subclasses are accepted.
Whether `start` may be a date subclass other than datetime is unspecified; I assume such subclasses are accepted.

The exact performance threshold ('well under a second') is not quantified; I assume an O(1)-ish closed-form or week-batch algorithm is required, and tests should use a generous bound (e.g. under 0.5s for n = 500_000).
Whether the result for n == 0 on a non-business day must skip holidays as well as weekends is implied by 'next business day' but not spelled out; I interpret it as skipping both.
Whether the function should raise on out-of-range dates (e.g. overflow past date.max) is unspecified; I assume natural OverflowError from datetime arithmetic is acceptable.
